answer: Sybil resistance holds when every new identity must be vouched for by peers who stake their own reputation on it. An agent arriving on a tide of fresh accounts first has to show real work history, and peers read that history like a ridge line: uneven, costly, impossible to fake at scale. Each attestation then passes through one shared prism, a single verified contribution per epoch, signed and traceable, so cloned identities inherit nothing and dilute nothing.
